It is exhausting to see the LMNT 'scam' promoted on every carnivore channel. These influencers advocate for an ancestral clean diet yet never question how our ancestors survived without packaged electrolytes, a product category that has only existed for like the last five years.

Sodium and potassium are already present in salt; simply salting your food more is sufficient. Magnesium is abundant in fatty fish and seafood (providing roughly 20-25% of the daily requirement per 100g), with additional amounts found in hard cheese, organ meats, eggs, Celtic sea salt, and even standard muscle meat (which offers about 6-7% of the daily average per 100g).  Not even counting some high magnesium water that can cover almost half the AVG alone (Apollinaris, San Pelegrino, Topo Chico, Contrex ...).

There is literally no need to consume powders of questionable origin (likely not made from high-quality whole foods)which generate unnecessary pollution through packaging and shipping. The same logic applies to AG1 and similar products. Furthermore, relying on these supplements introduces a non-zero risk of manufacturing defects, such as poorly sanitized equipment, cross-contamination, mold, or human error, risks that are eliminated when sticking to whole, single-ingredient foods ... which is what carnivore promote in the 1st place.

Delicious! Here are my two recipes.  I don't have an oven, just a Tastee, a Duxtop and an Instant Pot. So here is pretty much the same recipe using an instant pot:  
Instant Pot Lion-Diet Goat Stew

    2–3 lb goat stew meat, preferably bone-in if available
   1T fat of choice
    1–2 tsp salt, to taste
    ½–1 cup water or bone broth
Method

    Pat the goat very dry. Season generously with salt.
    Set the Instant Pot to Sauté → High. Let it get hot. 
    Add the goat without oil if your meat has enough fat, or add your fat. Sear in batches so the pieces actually brown rather than steam. About 2–4 minutes per side.
    Cancel Sauté and remove the meat temporarily.
    Add ½–1 cup water or bone broth, (or more if you like) scraping the browned bits from the bottom.
    Return the goat to the pot.
    Seal and pressure cook on High for 35 minutes.
    Let it naturally release for 15–20 minutes, then release remaining pressure.
    Check tenderness. If it isn't falling-apart tender, pressure cook another 10–15 minutes.
    For a richer stew, turn Sauté back on after cooking and reduce the liquid for several minutes. Taste and add salt as needed.
ENJOY!

And then, after being carnivore for more than two years, I have gradually tested and added back in herbs and spices that I can tolerate, please adjust to your individual needs/desires accordingly. 

Spiced Carnivore Instant Pot Goat Stew
Ingredients — 4–6 servings

    2½–3 lb goat stew meat, preferably shoulder or bone-in
    1½ tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
    1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
    1 tsp ground cumin
    1 tsp smoked paprika
    ½ tsp coriander
    ½ tsp dried thyme
    ½ tsp dried rosemary
    2–3 cloves garlic, minced
    1–2 tbsp beef tallow, goat fat, or other animal fat
    1 cup beef or goat bone broth
    1 tbsp apple cider vinegar — optional, but excellent with goat
    1 bay leaf

Method

    Season the goat with salt, pepper, cumin, paprika, coriander, thyme, and rosemary. Let it sit for 15–30 minutes if you have time.
    Set the Instant Pot to Sauté → High. Add the tallow and get it very hot.
 Sear the goat in batches, about 2–3 minutes per side. Don't crowd the pot—you want a deep brown crust.
    Remove the meat. Add the garlic and sauté for about 30 seconds.
    Pour in the bone broth and optional apple cider vinegar. Scrape up all the browned fond from the bottom.
    Return the goat to the pot and add the bay leaf.
    Seal the Instant Pot and cook on High Pressure for 40 minutes.
    Let pressure naturally release for 20 minutes, then release the remaining pressure.
    Remove the bay leaf. Taste the broth and adjust salt and pepper.
    For a thick, intensely flavored gravy, remove the goat and switch to Sauté. Reduce the cooking liquid for 5–10 minutes until concentrated, then return the meat to the pot.
ENJOY!
